entities.summary: Uta Ranke-Heinemann was a German theologian, academic, and author. In 1969, she was the first woman in the world to be habilitated in Catholic theology. She held a chair of ancient Church history and the New Testament at the University of Duisburg-Essen. When her license to teach was revoked by the bishop because of her critical position in matters of faith, the university created a nondenominational chair of History of Religion. Her 1988 book Eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven, criticising the Catholic Church's stance on women and sexuality, was published in several editions, and translated in 12 languages.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Uta Ranke-Heinemann's critical stance on women and sexuality led to her license being revoked, prompting the university to create a nondenominational chair of History of Religion. Her work had significant regional impact in Germany.
